additions.name: Data Center Nostrum Evergreen (DC Badajoz) - planned data centre with 300 MW grid access

status.summary: Data Riocaya, SLU plans the Data Center Nostrum Evergreen (DC Badajoz) in the Plataforma Logística del Suroeste Europeo, Badajoz. On 15 September 2026 the state gazette opened public information on its application for the SET Enlace 400/220 kV substation and a 292 m 400 kV line from Red Eléctrica's Riocaya substation, whose purpose is to connect "the future Data Center Nostrum Evergreen of 300 MW" to the transmission grid; the data centre itself is processed in separate files. On 7 September 2026 the regional gazette had published prior authorisation of its 220 kV consumption infrastructure. Neither record is development consent for the data centre, and no physical work is established.

locator.precision: Area centroid of the five Plataforma Logística del Suroeste Europeo plots (L.I-12, L.I-13, C.E.S-2, C.E.S-4 and C.E.S-4A; 22.27 ha) that Decreto 151/2025 names as the data-centre site. It locates the declared data-centre land, not a building footprint, the SE DC Badajoz or SET Enlace substations, an entrance or a surveyed boundary.
locator.identity_review: Decreto 151/2025 (DOE 17 November 2025) places the Data Riocaya, SLU data centre on plots L.I-12, L.I-13, C.E.S-2, C.E.S-4 and C.E.S-4A of the Plataforma Logística del Suroeste Europeo, 222,735 m2 in total. Catastro's address register describes exactly one urban parcel with each of these plot labels on PL Plataforma Logística, Badajoz: 3582902PD7038D (L.I-12, 34,235 m2), 3485901PD7038E (LI-13, 144,197 m2), 3485903PD7038E (C.E.S.-2, 16,695 m2), 3582905PD7038D (C.E.S.-4, 24,129 m2) and 3582904PD7038D (C.E.S.-4A, 3,478 m2). Their declared areas total 222,734 m2, 1 m2 short of the decree, and their INSPIRE geometries form one contiguous polygon whose area centroid lies inside LI-13; Catastro reverse lookup at the point confirms parcel 3485901PD7038E. The 2026 DOE authorisation sites the SE DC Badajoz substation in the logistics platform, and the BOE and DOE records name the same promoter and project. Neighbouring platform plots (L.I-1 to L.I-10, T.I, E.L.Z.V) are not part of the site.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Catastro publishes no positional accuracy for these boundaries. The point is a derived interior anchor of a 22.3 ha declared site whose farthest vertex is about 414 m away; no building layout is published.

additions.distinctness_review: Sites, projects, evidence (3,098 rows), the source records and the identity mapping of 2026-10-22-research-fortysecond (577 sites, 610 projects) were searched for Nostrum, Evergreen, Riocaya, Data Riocaya, Badajoz, Plataforma Logística and Suroeste Europeo: the only match is an unrelated Loudoun County parcel named Evergreen Meadows. No Atlas site lies within 2 km; the nearest are MERLIN Lisbon (170.0 km) and Start Campus Sines (190.5 km), and the nearest Spanish site is Meta Talavera de la Reina (219.9 km). No pending queue fragment or claim other than this one names Badajoz or Nostrum. The 2026-10-22 thirty-fourth holds held this candidate for want of plot references or plan geometry, which the Catastro plot records now supply; the 2026-10-16 thirty-first hold for IREN Badajoz (a planned 300 MW Badajoz, Extremadura site) may concern the same development, but no captured source links IREN to Data Riocaya or Nostrum Evergreen, so no IREN alias or role is recorded and IREN Badajoz must be screened against this record if it is reopened.
additions.successor_review: The BOE daily summaries for 29 July to 22 October 2026 and the DOE daily summaries for 29 July to 22 October 2026 (no issues on the 8 September and 12 October holidays) were scanned for data-centre, CPD, Nostrum and Riocaya titles: the only records are the 7 September DOE prior authorisation of the 220 kV infrastructure and the 15 September BOE notice. No environmental decision, development consent, municipal licence or works record for the data centre was found. Keep 15 September 2026 as the announcement observation.

additions.name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center — operating campus

status.summary: Meta's Building Texas page, published on 12 August 2026, describes its Fort Worth data center as operational since 2017 and names Fort Worth among the three Texas communities where its data centers support jobs, infrastructure and local organisations. An Internet Archive copy of 13 August 2026 contains the same statement, so the observation is the publication day. This supports an operating campus as of 12 August 2026; 2017 is the operator's stated start of operations and is not the observation. No capacity, IT load or new building is asserted.

locator.precision: Area centroid of Tarrant Appraisal District parcel 414K-3-7R2 (Alliance Gateway North Block 3 Lot 7R2, 4500 Like Way; 147.329 acres recorded, 145.77 geodesic acres, about 1.0 by 1.2 km), owned by Winner LLC and carrying the 2017 data-center improvements. It locates the operating campus parcel, not an individual building; the point lies inside the lot, 92 m from its boundary.
locator.identity_review: Meta names its Fort Worth Data Center (its first in Texas, ground broken 2015). Tarrant Appraisal District lists Winner LLC as owner of Lot 7R2 at 4500 Like Way with tax mail to 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park (Meta's headquarters), and personal-property accounts there mailed to 1 Meta Way and 1601 Willow Rd. City of Fort Worth permits on the lot name Facebook as owner (PE17-11410) and label the data-center buildings FTW3 to FTW6 for Winner LLC. The Tarrant County 911 address point for 4500 Like Way falls inside the lot. The adjacent QTS FTW1 campus at 14100 Park Vista Blvd (Lots 4R-1R3 to 4R-1R5, QTS entities) is a different operator's property and is excluded; Alliance as a whole and the Fort Worth city centre are not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The appraisal-district parcel polygons carry no published positional accuracy; the centroid represents a 147-acre campus parcel.

additions.distinctness_review: Searched sites, projects, evidence, source records and identity mapping of verified_construction_core/2026-10-22-research-fortyfirst and again, before finishing, of 2026-10-22-research-fortysecond, every pending queue fragment and claims.tsv, and all sources/*-holds.json for Meta Fort Worth, Facebook Fort Worth, Winner LLC, MMI Southwest, Like Way, 4500 Like, Alliance Gateway North and Project Ernst: no Atlas site, project or source names this campus. additions.successor_review: Meta's post sitemap (captured 22 October 2026) lists no Fort Worth item after 12 August; its later posts concern Ohio (31 August and 19 October), Kuna (3 September) and Eagle Mountain (14 September). The Fort Worth info sheet uploaded in September 2026 and the U.S. locations page modified on 2 October 2026 still present Fort Worth as an operating Meta data center. No closure, pause or new Fort Worth phase was found, and City of Fort Worth permit records on the lot show no newer filing after July 2024. The campus therefore stays operational as of 12 August 2026: 72 days before a 23 October 2026 update, inside the 85-day research window until 5 November and the 90-day admission window until 10 November 2026.

additions.name: Apple Prineville Data Center Campus — existing operations

status.summary: In the packet for its 13 October 2026 council meeting (generated 8 October), the City of Prineville's Resolution No. 1654 recites that Apple, Inc. owns and operates a data center within Prineville city limits, and the attached development agreement states that Apple owns and operates a data center campus on real property within the City. The council adopted the resolution unanimously on 13 October. This dated government record supports the operating status of Apple's existing Prineville campus. It does not state capacity, building count or opening dates, and the planned eastern campus expansion (the PRZ 06 development area) is not part of this status.

locator.precision: Centroid of the union of the three Crook County tax lots owned by Apple Inc (1515000000312, 1516070000101 and 1516070000102; 364.33 geodesic acres in one piece, about 1.8 by 1.6 km). It locates Apple's campus property as a whole, not an individual building; the existing building seen in county imagery lies about 0.6 km north-west of the point on lot 1515000000312, and the eastern lots are the PRZ 06 expansion area.
locator.identity_review: The resolution and agreement identify Apple's data-center campus within Prineville city limits and map it in Exhibit A as the APPLE CAMPUS north-east of Prineville Airport and east of the SW Connect Way buildings, beside SW Baldwin Road where the PRZ06 offsite lines end. The county tax-lot layer returns exactly three lots owned by Apple Inc there, all M1 Light Industrial, one with situs 1600 SW Baldwin Rd; together they form one contiguous holding, and the county's 2020 imagery shows a large data-centre-type building on lot 1515000000312. The separate multi-building campus on SW Connect Way (lots owned by Vitesse LLC, situs 735 and 500 SW Connect Way) and the large warehouse lots of LS Propdrop LLC on SW George Millican Rd are other owners' lots and are excluded. Prineville city centre, the airport and the situs label are not used as locators.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The county publishes no positional accuracy for its tax lots; the centroid represents a 364-acre holding about 1.8 km across.

status.summary: Start Campus's release of 21 October 2026 describes a digital-twin pilot focused on Nscale's operations within the SIN01 data center on the 1.2 GW SINES Data Campus, presented as a live AI factory environment. This confirms that the first building, SIN01, is operating on that date while the rest of the campus remains under development, so the campus stays partially operational. It says nothing about the capacity in service, SIN02 progress or the forecast deployment of more than 66,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.

status_updates.identity_review: Same campus as the existing record: the release names Start Campus's SINES Data Campus in Sines and its SIN01 building, the aliases already recorded for the imported Start Campus SINES data center campus (SINES DC, SINES Data Campus), whose partially operational status rests on SIN01 operating. The refresh keeps that campus-level scope; it does not touch the separate SIN02 construction project on the same site, add a phase or change the existing approximate locator.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 3 August 2026 observation, which came from an imported trade-press interview. The Start Campus media index captured on 22 October 2026 lists the 21 October release as its newest item; the 8 September (operator-of-the-year award) and 30 September (Sustainability Update 2025: SIN01's first full year of operation) releases report no pause or closure. No completion of SIN02 or of the full campus is asserted.

status.summary: On 8 July 2026 the Laramie County Board of Commissioners stated that the data-center development previously known as Project Jade, now Project Tembo, had received governing-body approvals for a zone change to the Switchgrass Industrial Park PUD and for its Commercial Site Plan; the county's Legistar record shows the Board granted the Project Jade site plan permit with conditions on 6 January 2026 (file 26-023). Crusoe has since withdrawn, and Google (d.b.a. Jupiter Star Holdings, LLC) has re-submitted a smaller Site Plan Revision (four buildings and 3,080,000 sq ft instead of five and 4,025,500 sq ft) that the county will process administratively. This supports permitted status for the data-centre development. No building permit, site works or construction of the data centre is established; the Tallgrass power hub works are a separate scope.
status.permit_reference: Laramie County Board of County Commissioners, 6 January 2026: approval with conditions of the Project Jade site plan permit (Legistar file 26-023, public hearing on the Project Jade site plan and the BFC Power and Cheyenne Power Hub site plans, Sections 5 and 7, T12N, R66W, 6th P.M.; minutes final 21 January 2026), on land rezoned to the Switchgrass Industrial Park PUD; Site Plan Revision PZ-26-00058 (Project Tembo, Jupiter Star Holdings, LLC) under administrative review as of 8 July 2026
status.permit_identity_review: The Board's motion grants the Project Jade site plan permit itself, the commercial site plan for the data-center development, separately from the power-hub site plan permit voted in the same item. Its conditions (agency comments, recorded easements, legal access, WYDOT approval) must be met before the county issues a Certificate of Review; they are later administrative steps, not a stay. The 8 July 2026 memo confirms the approvals and calls the Jade plan the previously approved Site Plan; it reports no appeal, revocation or lapse, and the Tembo revision reduces the approved scope rather than replacing the consent with a new application.

status_updates.identity_review: The existing record, imported from Tallgrass's 24 July 2025 release, is the Crusoe and Tallgrass AI data center campus near Cheyenne (Project Jade) in Laramie County, Wyoming, with Tallgrass's power supply. The county's 8 July 2026 memo names the same development, previously known as Project Jade and applied for by Crusoe Energy, with Tallgrass's Power Hub, and says it is now Project Tembo, re-submitted with Google (d.b.a. Jupiter Star Holdings, LLC) after Crusoe withdrew. Legistar file 26-023 places the Project Jade site plan in Sections 5 and 7, T12N, R66W (south of Cheyenne beside US 85, within about 5 km of the Colorado line). This is a status refresh of that one data-center development; the new developer is recorded in the summary only, and the record's inherited Laramie County centroid point, about 28 km north of these sections, is not changed here (a locator correction is held). The other Cheyenne-area Atlas records, Meta Cheyenne (about 12 km from these sections) and Related Digital Cheyenne (about 15 km), are different developments; the base identity mapping already separates Related Digital from the Jade/Switchgrass programme, and no record lies within 2 km of the sections.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the record's 24 July 2025 announced observation. Laramie County Legistar (queried 22 October 2026 for Tembo, Jupiter, Jade and Data Center) shows only the Planning Commission's postponement on 13 August (file 26-422) and approval on 10 September 2026 (file 26-466) of the Class B CUP for the Project Tembo HUB-1 Office Support Facility, an ancillary office use; no decision on the data-center Site Plan Revision appears there because it is administrative. The county's monthly building-permit reports for June, July and August 2026 list commercial permits by number and address only, so none can be attributed to the data center, and no site work, construction, pause or cancellation of the data center was found. Status is kept at permitted as of 8 July 2026.
